passages.provision_quote: Require all jurisdictional electric utilities (utilities) to offer a FIT to eligible customers (including persons that are not existing customers of the electric utility) not later than July 1, 2015.
passages.note: A feed-in tariff obliges utilities to buy renewable power at rates set to stimulate it, but sets no clean-energy share or binding shift (rung 1), is ratepayer- not publicly-funded (rung 2), and has only an interconnection-standards clause toward rung 3, so it shows the pro-clean-energy side only.
passages.actor_quote: Pierce January 15, 2014, read first time and referred to Committee on Utilities and Energy.

passages.note: Bill page names Pierce as author; same instrument as the bill text, which never got past referral to committee.
Says he promotes renewables and storage for utility competition; names no mandate, subsidy or permitting mechanism.
News excerpt reports that the forum covered environmental protections but contains none of his words on energy.

Current-campaign forum remarks: advocates renewables, rooftop solar and feed-in tariffs, but calls for no mandate with a deadline and no major public funding, so the rungs on the pro side are not separated.

rows.reasoning: His authorship of HB 1374 (2014), a feed-in tariff bill, and his words ("a relentless advocate for renewable energy and moving us to a clean energy economy") place him on the pro-clean-energy side. Neither the bill nor his words match every clause of one rung: the bill sets no clean-energy share to meet by a firm deadline ("Require a shift to clean energy through mandates and firm deadlines"), it is not public money ("major subsidies, tax credits, and public investment"), and it has no permitting-reform clause.

quotes.text: And I've been a relentless advocate for renewable energy and moving us to a clean energy economy.
And so I'm doing everything I can to push us to promote solar, rooftop solar.
I fought these bills and have advocated for more competition in the utility industry by promoting renewable energy like wind and solar, along with energy storage.
